questions.question: In Y = β₀ + β₁X + ε, what does β₁ represent?
options: The fitted mean of Y when X = 0
The fitted change in mean Y for a one-unit increase in X
questions.explanation: The slope β₁ describes the fitted change in the mean response for a one-unit change in the feature.

questions.question: In the same model, what does β₀ represent?
options: The fitted mean of Y at X = 0
questions.explanation: The intercept is the fitted mean response when X equals zero, though zero may be outside the observed range.

questions.question: Ordinary least squares chooses the line to minimise which quantity?
questions.explanation: OLS minimises the sum of squared differences between observed and fitted values.

questions.question: For observed y = 9 and predicted ŷ = 11, residual = observed − predicted. What is the residual?
options: −2; the prediction is two units too high
+2; the prediction is two units too low
−2; the prediction is two units too low
questions.explanation: 9 − 11 = −2. A negative residual means the prediction was above the observed value.

questions.question: On a particular evaluated dataset, R² = 0 indicates that the model's squared error is:
options: Equal to the squared error from predicting the dataset mean
Always less than the mean baseline
questions.explanation: R² = 1 − SSE/SST, so zero means the model has the same squared error as the mean-only baseline on that scored dataset.

questions.question: Assuming non-constant targets, ordinary least squares evaluated on its own training rows with an intercept can have negative R².
questions.explanation: With an intercept, OLS on the same training rows can at least match the mean-only baseline, so training R² is nonnegative.

questions.question: A model's R² on held-out test data can be negative.
questions.explanation: On test data, the fitted model can perform worse than the mean baseline used by the R² calculation.

questions.question: A residual-versus-fitted plot shows a clear U-shaped pattern. What is the best next interpretation?
options: The pattern suggests the straight-line form may miss structure
The model proves that X causes Y
questions.explanation: A curve is a diagnostic reason to investigate the model form; it does not prove causation or identify a single cause.

questions.question: With an intercept, the fitted simple OLS line passes through which point?
questions.explanation: The OLS normal equations imply that the fitted line passes through the sample means when an intercept is included.

questions.question: In scikit-learn, what shape should X have for one feature and five samples?
questions.explanation: Scikit-learn expects a two-dimensional feature matrix: rows are samples and columns are features.
